subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_search — full-text search over the agent's own session transcripts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core lexical `sessions_search` tool and `sessions.search` gateway method backed by a session transcript index, or should transcript recall remain in the existing memory/search and UI-specific paths for now?
rationale: The capability is missing, but adding it changes core agent-tool surface, gateway API surface, persisted per-agent indexes, and transcript privacy boundaries; repository policy requires human product/security direction for that scope.

options.title: Approve Core Search Seam
options.body: Define and implement a bounded core `sessions.search` plus `sessions_search` contract with visibility, redaction, index lifecycle, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Route Through Memory/UI First
options.body: Keep exact transcript search out of core for now and treat existing memory-search or UI-specific work as the supported path.

options.title: Defer For Security Design
options.body: Hold implementation until maintainers specify retention, snippet redaction, access scope, backfill, and pruning rules.

recommendation.title: Approve Core Search Seam
recommendation.body: Define and implement a bounded core `sessions.search` plus `sessions_search` contract with visibility, redaction, index lifecycle, and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened the maintainer-labeled request and have recent session-control history across the affected product surfaces.
